name: NA62 detector

placements.locator: arXiv:1703.08501 (commissioning from 2014); be-dep-ea.web.cern.ch/northarea (ECN3 currently houses NA62)

technology.value: Decay-in-flight kaon spectrometer: beam-tracking (GigaTracker), ring-imaging Cherenkov (RICH) particle identification, liquid-krypton (LKr) electromagnetic calorimeter and photon/particle veto systems around a large vacuum vessel

intervals.label: operating
intervals.note: Physics data taking from Run 1 (2016-2018) through the ongoing Run 2 (2021-present); see experiment:na62 for the full run-by-run breakdown.

gigatracker_track_time_resolution.note: GigaTracker beam-spectrometer timing resolution on reconstructed tracks (single-hit resolution is below 200 ps). Display leads with the stored unit (ns) to satisfy the A21 display/value cross-check, with the source's own wording (65 ps) alongside it.

description.value: Low-mass, high-intensity silicon-pixel beam spectrometer providing 4D (position + time) tracking of individual beam particles at flux up to 2.0 MHz/mm^2, with 65 ps time resolution on tracks
description.quote: a low mass high intensity beam 4D tracker with 65 ps time resolution on tracks

summary.plain: The NA62 detector is a long chain of instruments in an underground hall at CERN, built to spot a positive kaon turning into a pion and two invisible neutrinos. A precise beam tracker, a ring-shaped light detector and a calorimeter work together to reject almost everything else.
summary.technical: Decay-in-flight spectrometer in the ECN3 cavern: GigaTracker beam-timing spectrometer (65 ps track time resolution, up to 2.0 MHz/mm^2 flux), RICH counter, LKr electromagnetic calorimeter, straw trackers and hermetic photon/particle veto systems, built 2009-2014 and operating since 2015.

notes: Placed at site:cern-ecn3-north-area, created by this same workstream.

Detector-paper PDF (cds.cern.ch mirror) was blocked by a bot-detection challenge in this session; specs beyond the GigaTracker figures confirmed via a separate arXiv subsystem paper were not independently re-verified against the full JINST text and are therefore limited to what the abstract/search-indexed text stated.
